text: What is the primary purpose of the controlling process in an organization?
options: To ensure that the organization achieves its goals and objectives.
To make decisions about the organization's future.
To evaluate the performance of the organization.
To motivate employees to work harder.
correctAnswer: To ensure that the organization achieves its goals and objectives.
explanation: Controlling is the process of ensuring that the organization achieves its goals and objectives. It involves comparing actual performance with planned performance and taking corrective action when necessary. This helps to ensure that the organization stays on track and achieves its desired outcomes.
subject: Business Studies

A method of controlling where only critical points are controlled.
A method of controlling where no points are controlled.
A method of controlling where all points are controlled.
correctAnswer: A method of controlling where only critical points are controlled.
explanation: Critical Point Control (CPC) is a method of controlling where only critical points are controlled. This involves identifying the most important points in the organization and controlling them closely. This helps to ensure that the organization achieves its goals and objectives.

text: What is the relationship between planning and controlling?
options: Planning is a part of controlling.
Controlling is a part of planning.
Planning and controlling are two separate processes.
Planning and controlling are interdependent processes.
correctAnswer: Planning and controlling are interdependent processes.
explanation: Planning and controlling are interdependent processes. Planning involves setting goals and objectives, while controlling involves ensuring that the organization achieves those goals and objectives. Controlling is based on the plans that have been set, and it involves comparing actual performance with planned performance.

text: What is the purpose of variance analysis in controlling?
options: To identify areas where performance is deviating from planned performance.
To identify areas where performance is better than planned performance.
To identify areas where performance is worse than planned performance.
To identify areas where performance is the same as planned performance.
correctAnswer: To identify areas where performance is deviating from planned performance.
explanation: Variance analysis is a technique used in controlling to identify areas where performance is deviating from planned performance. This involves comparing actual performance with planned performance and identifying the differences. This helps to identify areas where corrective action is needed.
